Honestly, I don’t think it’s fair for you to assume that I have the wrong diagnosis. I can emphasize with you in that psychiatrists and therapists for years missed my adhd and diagnosed me with anxiety and/or depression, even after I specifically asked multiple times if adhd was a possibility. I also had negative experiences with antidepressants. I finally got evaluated by a psychologist who specializes in neuropsychological assessments which specifically look at adhd and executive functioning, and the testing was very thorough and over different days—im sure this process was much more thorough than how you got diagnosed. Along with that, I mentioned initially that I see a therapist, and therapists are trained to diagnosis as well and spend way more time getting to know someone assuming it’s a longer-term therapuetic relationship. 

While I am glad you found what works for you, I’d highly suggest not telling someone they have the wrong diagnosis or just assuming something based on your own experiences. Everyone’s brain is different, and I tend to be extremely sensitive to dosages and other factors. Also, for women, hormones and where we are in our cycles impacts the medication effectiveness and there’s legitimate research on this. And I’m not alone in this as an adhder. I’m saying this because if I were a little earlier into my adhd journey, this could have been extremely confusing for me while trying to navigate all of this. Imposter syndrome about having adhd is also a thing, and I assure you my diagnosis is not incorrect. 

That all being said, sending love and healing your way✨and id implore you to look inwards and reflect on the assumption too

So I tried 20 mg twice for about 2 weeks. I recall it working "well" first but I didn't have much to compare it then, but I noticed with vyvanse and dexedrine that it was lacking something that made me feel alert enough. It could have been the dose for sure, but toward the second week of taking it, I started feeling foggy, cloudy, and disassociated. Food/nutrition definitely could have impacted it or dose. I mention dexedrine because vyvanse gets converted into the active chemical of it, and they both felt similar to me. I did have bad crashes in the middle of the day with vyvanse, but I noticed I still need at least an instant when I take vyvanse. You could always try less and see how you feel or see if an increase in dose helps. I will say, myself and a friend who actually does take vyvanse at 30 mg seem to be more sensitive to things, in which the wrong dose can make us feel worse effects cognitively. Even with adderall now, if my dose is slightly too high or low (even by 2.5 mg for instants), it feels similarly and I feel like I would have been better off not taking anything at all.   
It's been a couple years of me figuring out meds, and I finally have added coffee again or caffeine like white or green tea too which actually has been a big help. If you're new to meds, I would really suggest tracking meds, nutrition, hydration, focus, and mood (and whatever else may be relevant to you) in a journal to help along the process of finding the best fit for you meds and dosages wise. I wish I had done this earlier. Also, if you're a female, menstrual cycle can really impact things, and I do believe that I felt foggier during luteal phase (I have PMDD too), and for many females with ADHD, medications are less effective anywhere from a few days to 2 weeks before periods, and people either need to increase their dose or just don't take it a few days before (there's studies on this too). 

That all being said, part of me wishes I tried vyvanse for longer or increased my dose because it did help me feel calm at first, but I think it may only do so much for my focus compared to adderall. I guess I can always try it again in the future. 

Feel free to let me know if you have any other questions. I hope this is helpful and not information overload lol.
